title: Seek Solitude
coreMove: Choose solitude that removes the audience long enough for honest thought, then judge the practice by how clearly and kindly you return to people waiting outside.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse solitude with disappearance
exampleSpecs.stakes: a retreat can either clarify life or become a romantic excuse to avoid it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two named people use Thoreau, Walden Pond, 1845, and Concord to distinguish solitude from quitting people

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who expect solitude to produce a dramatic announcement
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may mistake visible output for better judgment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: set up a Bill Gates Think Week expectation, then reveal a quieter result

exampleSpecs.audience: workers whose quiet blocks get pulled back into group demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: a short solo hour can either become protected thought or another public performance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: compress the Bill Gates Think Week idea into a phone exchange about protecting 30 minutes

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose first quiet minutes get invaded by alerts
exampleSpecs.stakes: the routine can be rescued only if the interruption is handled physically
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A reading scene changes the room when the first interruption arrives.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who expect solitude to feel grand
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small room can teach the body before any large insight arrives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one lived detail uses Henry David Thoreau and Walden Pond without turning the scene into a decision

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who copy retreat language while keeping the same digital crowd
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team must locate why the offsite produced a reactive memo
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A product lead learns that a solitude practice cannot keep live audience channels open.
